title: Update PRD: autoscale warm-pool, deterministic fallbacks, and rollout gates after coldstart outage
creator: Priya Rao
description: Summary: During the 2026-02-05 coldstart/autoscaler incident the serving fleet experienced a 3x latency spike and sustained error rate increases for 18 minutes while autoscale pools and model cache warmed. The postmortem identified two primary product gaps: (1) PRD lacks explicit warm-pool and pre-warming requirements for Dedicated and Hosted autoscale paths, and (2) no deterministic fallback policy with clear rollout gates exists in the PRD for runtime degradation scenarios. Objective: Update the runtime PRD to add measurable requirements for warm-pools, pre-warming behavior, deterministic fallback model selection, and rollout gates tied to runbooks and automated acceptance tests. The scope covers PRD wording, acceptance criteria, required telemetry, and an explicit rollout plan and rollback criteria for runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: Warm-pool requirement: PRD defines a baseline warm-pool size formula (min_instances = max(2, ceil(request_qps / 50))) and an option for customer-configurable min_instances for Dedicated tenants.

Pre-warm behavior: PRD specifies that autoscaler must maintain a 'warm_percent' state that keeps GPUs with loaded KV cache for the top N models (N default 3) and that coldstart time for a 2-context request must be < 450ms median and < 900ms 95th in synthetic load tests.

Deterministic fallback policy: PRD mandates a fallthrough sequence with deterministic priority rules (local-cache model variant -> quantized variant -> cross-region fallback -> degraded-latency mode) and tie-breakers defined by cost tier and customer-configured SLA tier.

Runbook gates: PRD introduces two automated gates before global rollout: (A) automated chaos/scale test (passes 95th latency SLO on synthetic replay) and (B) incident-simulator acceptance tests that run for 24h with no more than 2 transient error spikes > 2x baseline.

Observability & alerts: PRD lists required metrics (warm_pool_utilization, coldstart_latency_p50/p95, fallback_activation_count, model_variant_switch_rate) and alert thresholds; each metric must be instrumented and visible in Console dashboards before rollout.

Acceptance tests: end-to-end CI job that replays a sampled 1h production trace and validates coldstart latency and failed-call rates against the SLOs; test artifacts and dashboard links must be included in PRD.

Rollout and rollback criteria: PRD contains explicit canary steps (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with SLO gates; rollback criteria include a persistent p95 latency increase > 15% for 10 minutes or error rate > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
Documentation & customer communication: PRD must include a migration note for Dedicated customers explaining min_instance impacts and an admin Console control to opt into pre-warm settings.
Security & compliance: PRD requires review of KMS impact for any pre-warm cache of customer keys; security_review_required flag must be set if customer-managed keys are affected.
decisions: Adopted a conservative default warm-pool sizing formula (see acceptance criteria) to balance cost and latency; Dedicated tenants can override.
Deterministic fallback will be explicit in PRD and implemented in runtime as a policy object with priority order; runtime team to expose variant priorities via API.
Rollout will be staged with canary percentages and automated incident-simulator acceptance tests prior to each stage; Console will show rollout state and gate pass/fail reasons.
Telemetry owners: Observability team (ENG-4123) will own metric instrumentation and dashboard templates; Product to validate completeness before rollout.
We will require the CI replay acceptance tests to run in pre-merge mode for all PRs touching autoscaler/fallback code paths.
